plan.title: feat(authz): closed-verb release gates + AFK templates consuming human-origin grants (#1095 slim)

narratives.Description: Wave 4 of epic #2948. Slim delivery of #1095: release-class closed-verb gates and AFK session-auth *templates* that mint/consume Wave 1 human-origin grants (packages/core authz). Do NOT invent a second mint path or parallel session-auth SoT that agents can self-satisfy. Rebase on TS engine + hooks/runtimeAuthority. Full #871 finish-loop product is Wave 5 — out of scope here. Non-verb product-edit provenance stays Wave 1.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator cutting a release or AFK high-blast verb, I want release-publish and peer closed verbs to fail closed unless a human-origin grant or DEFT_ALLOW_* bypass is present, so that agents cannot treat prose or self-authored lifecycle state as publish authority.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Step 1: Add conventions/verb-classification.json (or content/contracts sibling) with release-cut, release-publish, release-rollback rows: closure_set, explicit_required, irreversibility, wildcard_allowed=false, skill/phase pointer. Step 2: TS pure classifier evaluateClosedVerb(verb, target, {grants, env}) that allows only when (a) DEFT_ALLOW_<VERB>=1 ephemeral bypass, or (b) matching human-origin grant with operations covering the verb (map release-publish/deployment-class ops), or (c) explicit authz template grant id. Step 3: Wire release-publish (and release cut entry if clean) to call the classifier before draft->public; fail closed with structured code. Step 4: AFK templates via authz:grant presets (e.g. --template release-publish --target vX.Y.Z) that only call existing mintGrant / operator-cli origin — no second store under session-auth as independent authority (optional mirror file OK if it only references grant ids). Step 5: task verify:verb-classification or content-contract tests; CHANGELOG cites #1095 #2948. Out of scope: #871 finish-loop PR-C, HMAC, Python-only preflight universe as sole gate, full PR-D post-session audit. drive-to: merge-ready.

items.title: TS closed-verb evaluator consumes Wave 1 grants

narrative.Acceptance: evaluateClosedVerb returns allow only when DEFT_ALLOW_* is set or a matching human-origin grant satisfies the verb target and rejects agent-authored or missing grants with a stable deny code.

items.title: release-publish fails closed without grant or bypass

narrative.Acceptance: When no grant and no DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH, release-publish fails closed before draft-to-public and when a matching operator-cli grant is present the gate returns allow.
